page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The Queen of Sheba
title: The Queen of Sheba
description:
Anna is still getting used to how things work in her new job. She turns to her colleagues to ask for help, but upsets Denise by sounding too bossy.
This episode explores language you can use to make polite requests.
phrases: I was wondering if you could do something for me...
Would you be able to print out a file for me?
Could I have it within ten minutes please?
Could you possibly help me with the printer?
Would you mind writing your email later?

listening_challenge.question: What reason does Tom give for being too busy to help Anna with her printer?
listening_challenge.answer: Tom says he has to send an email to a client.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to English at Work. We're still in Anna's first week in the busy offices of Tip Top Trading. How's it going Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Everything's still so new to me. I keep needing to ask people for help!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, that's only natural at the beginning. To ask people politely for help use the words would and could. You can also use the word please, but don't make the mistake of thinking's enough to make what you say polite.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Er, ok.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hello Anna!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh hi, Paul!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I was wondering if you could do something for me?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes of course.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text:
Would you be able to print out a file for me? It's a document on CBL – Convincing Bananas Limited – they're one of our suppliers. The file should
be on the system and could I have it in the next ten minutes please, as they're on their way here for a meeting?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. Oh no, I've no idea how to find it! Tom...?!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Er, ask Denise. She should know.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Ok, thanks Tom, I'll ask her.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: (on the phone to Sharon) I'd warned her, you know, I said 'Victoria, if you don't change your hairdresser

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Denise?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: One day you'll… hold on a moment. Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Please email me the background file on CBL.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Er!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text:
(on the phone) Who does that girl think she is?... Anna... new girl... I told you about her... yes with the saucepans, that's the one. She's only been
here five minutes and she's already acting like the Queen of Sheba...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh and Denise, please send it to me within five minutes, Paul needs it soon. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Really!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: He he, good to see who's the boss, eh Denise?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Really!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Er, Anna, I think you've upset Denise...?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Upset Denise?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You were a bit rude when you asked her to help.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Was I?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Remember what I said Anna. Just using ‘please’ to ask someone to do something can sound a little rude.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Instead of saying 'Please send me the file' you could say 'Could you possibly send me the file?' or 'Would you mind sending me the file?'

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh! English is so confusing! I'll try to remember that. Oh no, the printer isn't even set up! Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Please help me with…I mean, could you possibly help me with the printer?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Er... I need to finish this email to a really important new client.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But it's really urgent. Would you mind writing your email later?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Okay, since you asked so nicely. Let's have a look...

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Well, it's a good thing Anna has understood how to use 'could' and 'would' to ask for things, before she upsets anyone else. Let's hear those phrases
again:

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text:
I was wondering if you could do something for me?
Would you be able to print out a file for me?
Could I have it within ten minutes please?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text:
Could you possibly help me with the printer?
Would you mind writing your email later?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: The printer seems to be working well, but how well are Anna and Denise working together? Are these two going to be enemies?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Really! 'Denise do this! Denise do that!' I'm telling you Sharon, I've almost had enough! I get treated like I'm some kind of servant!
